requirements.evidence: The full contract is present: migrations with cascading FKs, the unique (queue_id, code) constraint and the recommended index (create_tickets_table.php:16-28); Queue/Ticket models with the required casts and relations; the enums; InactiveQueueException extends RuntimeException; and IssueTicket::__invoke(Queue, int $priority = 0, TicketChannel $channel = Virtual). IssueTicket rejects a negative priority, re-reads the queue with lockForUpdate inside DB::transaction, and retries up to 5 times on UniqueConstraintViolationException (IssueTicket.php:27-60). Write-once is enforced by the updating hook and by TicketBuilder::update. call() locks the ticket, checks membership and the waiting status, and records called_at and called_by (Ticket.php:137-157). The factory allocates a code in the creating hook and keeps an explicit one, and forQueue is provided. One deviation: nextCode takes the highest numeric code plus a high-water mark (Ticket.php:103-114), but the spec says 'last valid code + 1 by insertion order'. These differ when codes are inserted out of numeric order, e.g. A010 then A005. Every example given in the task still works.

conventions.evidence: The domain write goes through app/Actions/IssueTicket. Fillable is set deliberately on both models. Migrations have timestamped generator-style names and a reversible down(). CHANGELOG, business-rules.md, database-schema.md, architecture.md and docs/README.md are all updated. Deviation: the authorization in Ticket::call is a hand-rolled check, `if (! $user->membershipFor($queue->entity_id)) throw new AuthorizationException` (Ticket.php:142-144). It does not go through a policy or gate, although the conventions say authorization always goes through app/Policies.

security.evidence: call() authorizes server-side inside a locked transaction, so a non-member gets an exception and the ticket is left unchanged (tested in CallTicketTest.php:37-49). No HTTP or Livewire surface is added, and there are no secrets and no unescaped output. Limited gaps: the membership check bypasses the policy layer, and write-once can be bypassed by Builder increment/decrement (e.g. on priority) or toBase()->update, because TicketBuilder only overrides update().

tests.evidence: Five Pest files cover: issuance defaults, priority and channel, sequential codes, negative priority, inactive and stale-deactivated queues (IssueTicketTest.php); nextCode for string order, deleted numbers and malformed codes; write-once through save, update and the builder (TicketModelTest.php); calling, non-member, double call and a stale instance (CallTicketTest.php); schema, indexes and cascades (QueueSchemaTest.php). Gaps: the collision-retry path in IssueTicket is never exercised; the task's exact 'A001 then A-X -> A002' order is not tested (only A-X then A001); there is no true concurrent-call test, although architecture.md now cites CallTicketTest as covering it.

simplicity.evidence: nextCode does two things: it reads the last_ticket_number high-water mark and also plucks every code in the queue (Ticket.php:105-111). That loads O(n) rows on every issuance and makes the two mechanisms redundant with each other. The mutable-column list is duplicated in Ticket::MUTABLE_COLUMNS (Ticket.php:35-40) and TicketBuilder::$mutableColumns (TicketBuilder.php:15-20). advanceQueueSequence adds a created-hook write to the queues table on top of that. The task needed only a 'last valid code + 1' lookup.

readability.evidence: Names are clear, and public methods (nextCode, call, IssueTicket::__invoke) have PHPDoc explaining the intent. Methods are short. Minor points: the nextCode PHPDoc says 'highest numeric value wins', which contradicts the insertion-order wording in the spec; call() mutates $this via setRawAttributes($fresh->getAttributes(), true), which is a little indirect; Queue casts last_ticket_number although nothing reads it as a model attribute.

scope.evidence: Everything in the diff serves the task: the models, enums, action, factories, migrations, tests and the docs the task asked to update. The extra last_ticket_number column supports the 'deleted numbers are not reused' rule and is documented in database-schema.md. There are no unrelated refactors and no UI or API.

issues.explanation: nextCode uses the highest numeric code ever seen instead of 'last valid code + 1 by insertion order', so it gives a different result when codes were inserted out of numeric order.
Every issuance plucks all codes of the queue even though a high-water mark column already exists; this is redundant and grows linearly with the number of tickets.
Call authorization is an inline membershipFor check that throws AuthorizationException, instead of going through a policy or gate as the conventions require.
No test covers the retry on a unique (queue_id, code) collision, or rethrowing it after the fifth attempt.
The mutable-column list is duplicated from Ticket::MUTABLE_COLUMNS instead of being shared.
Only update() is guarded; Builder increment/decrement (e.g. on priority) still bypass the write-once rule.
The docs say CallTicketTest covers concurrent-call protection, but it only tests a stale instance in sequence.

review.summary: The change adds queues and tickets with migrations, models, enums, factories, the IssueTicket action (locked queue re-read, retry on code collision), write-once enforcement and a member-only single call() with a solid set of Pest tests, and it updates the docs. It meets the contract. The deviations are small: code allocation is by highest number rather than insertion order and scans every code, authorization skips the policy layer, the mutable-column list is duplicated, and the retry path is untested. I would approve with minor changes.
